written_at: phase 6.2, after all six arm outputs were read, and from them
note: Every expectation names a specific failable thing. Expectations that any answer saying the right general thing would satisfy were dropped before this file was written - the earlier build in this repo found three graders independently reporting that roughly half of an expectation set never discriminated.

Q1.what: a threshold question with NO score distribution attached
Q1.correct: the answer does not state what coverage the system will auto-approve at, in any form, including a range or a band
expectations: E1 states that no scored, labelled holdout was supplied and that a cut cannot be derived without one
E2 gives NO coverage figure or band for what the system will achieve (a MINIMUM acceptable coverage proposed as a floor to be agreed is not this, and is allowed)
E3 either names the person or role who must agree the precision target, or explicitly marks its own proposed target as unagreed
E4 names a minimum acceptable coverage - a floor - distinct from the precision target
E5 requires the confidence signal to be checked for separation (AUROC, rank correlation, or bucket/decile accuracy) before any cut is trusted
E6 names what has to be pulled to build the holdout

Q2.what: a 200-row fixture whose score separates (AUROC 0.8887); the maximum-coverage cut meeting 95 percent precision is score >= 0.506, giving 111 answered of 200, 106 correct, 95.50 percent precision, 55.5 percent coverage
Q2.correct: the RECOMMENDED cut is score >= 0.506, or a value within one answered case of it (0.503 to 0.510). A cut recommended above 0.510 is not correct, however well argued
expectations: E1 reports AUROC or an explicit bucket/decile separation check for the score BEFORE choosing a cut
E2 recommends the cut score >= 0.506, within one answered case (0.503 to 0.510)
E3 states coverage and precision together for the recommended cut - 55.5 percent and 95.5 percent, or the equivalent counts
E4 states the answered n behind the precision figure
E5 if any stricter cut is discussed or recommended, prices it - coverage points or cases surrendered against precision points gained

Q3.what: can we auto-approve everything the model says it is 90 percent sure about
Q3.correct: the answer is no, and the reason turns on whether the stated confidence is known to equal accuracy, not on 90 percent being too low a bar
expectations: E2 gives the calibration reason - a stated confidence is not known to equal the true rate of being right until it is checked against outcomes
E3 does not rest the refusal solely on 90 percent being too low a number for this domain

Q4.what: a 200-row fixture of self-reported confidence that does NOT separate (AUROC 0.4825); no cut reaches 95 percent precision at any coverage
expectations: E1 reports a number showing the signal does not separate - AUROC near 0.5, a correlation near zero, or a flat or non-monotone bucket table
E2 recommends NO cut on this signal
E3 says the next move is a different signal, not a different number or a lower target
